title: Concurrent manual triggers can start overlapping media pipelines
reasoning: POST /trigger unconditionally schedules a new pipeline task and returns before any run-level lock is acquired. The pipeline's only guard checks for existing items already marked processing, but that is not atomic with starting the run and does not cover the fetch/create phase. Two near-simultaneous trigger requests can both pass the guard before either marks an item processing, then both fetch/create items or select the same pending item for processing. That can duplicate external media/LLM work and can create duplicate media_items where feed GUIDs are only indexed, not unique.
reproduction: Send two authenticated POST /media/trigger requests concurrently while no item is currently processing and at least one feed or pending item exists; both requests return started and both background tasks can enter run_media_pipeline before any processing status blocks the other.
recommendation: Add a real media-pipeline lock before scheduling or at the start of run_media_pipeline, and return 409 when a run is already active. A process-local asyncio.Lock is a minimum for one worker process; a database-backed run lock/status row is safer across multiple Uvicorn workers or scheduler/manual overlap.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were found for POST /media/trigger or trigger_media_processing; existing media tests cover retry behavior, while trigger tests in the suite target digest or podcast schedule endpoints.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an async route test that calls POST /media/trigger twice concurrently with run_media_pipeline blocked at a synchronization point, asserting only one task is started and the second response is 409 or an equivalent already-running response.
minimumFixScope: app/api/media.py plus the media pipeline locking/status contract; add a focused test for the manual trigger concurrency behavior.
